title: A Blood Glucose Control Framework Based on Reinforcement Learning With Safety and Interpretability: In Silico Validation
reviewer_a_notes: Planning is demonstrated only in the UVA/Padova in-silico environment. Fifty-step imagined trajectories are used for learning, but performance is not reported as a function of rollout horizon. PID guides early training and is a control baseline, not an action-agnostic dynamics comparator. No formal uncertainty calibration or external cohort is reported.
reviewer_b_notes: Closed-loop simulator utility and safety are strong, but learned dynamics have only a fixed 30-minute error test; no calibration, action ablation, external validation, or public artifacts.
reviewer_a_anchors: Official IEEE Access PDF, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2021.3100007: pp. 5-9 define the extended state, random-forest glucose transition model, 30-min prediction target, and safe-SAC actions; pp. 12-16 and Tables 3-5 report recursive prediction errors and 20-day closed-loop outcomes; Figs. 6-10 show virtual-subject control and safety behavior.
reviewer_b_anchors: Methods Sec. III, Figs. 1–2, Algorithms 1–3; Experiments Sec. IV-A–C, Tables 1–2, Figs. 3–4; Appendix A.

title: A data-driven Alzheimer's disease progression simulator for retrospective validation and prospective Phase III power design.
reviewer_a_notes: The paper implements intervention-conditioned trial simulations and explicit treated-versus-placebo endpoint/power calculations. Trial-specific and leave-one-trial-out calibration means the external trial comparison is not a fully frozen independent validation. Repeated simulations quantify Monte Carlo variation, but no reliability, coverage, or calibration-slope analysis is reported. Public source code is identified in the paper.
reviewer_b_notes: Six placebo/treatment profiles and power simulations support action evidence. External RCT comparison is adapted with trial-specific calibration, so it is not frozen; safety and full causal identification remain absent.
reviewer_a_anchors: medRxiv full text, DOI 10.64898/2026.05.03.26352317: Abstract and pp. 2-4 state the six-trial retrospective/prospective design; Results pp. 5-11, Tables 1-2, and Figs. 1-5 report biomarker trajectories, placebo/treatment contrasts, endpoint predictions, and power curves; Methods pp. 14-21 define the VAE-neural-ODE state and amyloid-clearance intervention; pp. 13-14 discuss limitations.
reviewer_b_anchors: Abstract; Methods pp. 6–16 and Algorithm 1; Results/trial figures pp. 17–27; code/data statements.

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
reviewer_a_notes: This is strong within-simulator planning evidence with baseline containment, multiple policy perturbations and constraints. Causal evidence is partial because the estimand and matched random streams are explicit only within an assumed synthetic system; no real-hospital identification or external validation exists. Safety is a constraint/stress proxy, not clinical safety.
reviewer_b_notes: The causal/policy contrast is fully defined inside a known synthetic simulator, hence causal evidence is strong for that simulated data-generating process but does not establish real-hospital effects. The learned predictor is fixed-horizon, not shown consuming its own generated states recursively. Frozen validation is synthetic zero-shot shift.
reviewer_a_anchors: medRxiv v1 Methods: synthetic hospital, H=7 graph forecasting, matched policy branches and MILP; Results report stress tests, held-out action-ranking accuracy/regret/non-worsening; official predictive and causal GitHub repositories.
reviewer_b_anchors: Preprint Methods define the synthetic 10-ward/200-patient/300-staff hospital, T=7/H=7 prediction, partial surveillance, five-policy branch, common deterministic noise, and constrained optimization; Results report surveillance and distribution-shift stress tests and policy ranking; equation defines ΔB7(a)=B7(baseline)-B7(a).

title: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease Clinical Trial Simulator: Case Reports of Model-Informed Drug Development.
reviewer_a_notes: Alternative assumed treatment effects are simulated against placebo to support trial-design decisions. The disease models have prior test/VPC support, but intervention response is hypothetical rather than clinically validated, and no confounding or overlap analysis supports causal interpretation. The public Shiny interface and snippets aid inspection but do not constitute a complete downloadable analysis repository.
reviewer_b_notes: Placebo plus parameter-effect scenarios support action testing and trial utility, but treatment effects are imposed rather than empirically validated; external, causal, safety, and calibration evidence are absent.
reviewer_a_anchors: Clinical and Translational Science full text, DOI 10.1002/psp4.70258: Methods sections 'Development of the CTS tool' and 'Clinical trial simulations' describe the UMOD/MUC1 registry models, synthetic cohorts, placebo and treatment parameter changes, durations, and 100 replicates; Results case reports and associated figures/tables report power across effect sizes and trial designs; Discussion states assumptions and validation limits; Data S1 supplies selected code examples.
reviewer_b_anchors: Model/Methods and Fig. 1; case studies and Figs./Tables 2–5; Discussion and Data S1.

title: Chreode: A Cell World Model for One-Step Temporal Dynamics and Perturbation Prediction
reviewer_a_notes: The action-conditioned claim is supported by architecture and perturbation transfer, but developmental pretraining uses a null action and no action-removal, shuffle, dose, or causal test. Frozen external validation refers only to the zero-shot Weinreb fate analysis; the time-transition and GEARS tasks involve downstream training.
reviewer_b_notes: Highest claim is action-conditioned because the paper defines a nominal intervention-conditioned transition and perturbation task. However, the action token is null during temporal pretraining and the Norman result replaces a GEARS embedding rather than evaluating a standalone action-conditioned Chreode operator. Multiple elapsed-time targets are one-step queries, not free-running rollout. Cross-dataset results use fine-tuning, so external evidence is adapted rather than frozen. The do(a) notation triggers causal scrutiny, but no effect contrast, identification strategy, overlap analysis, or counterfactual validation is provided. Qualitative dual-use discussion supports safety=1 without a hazard test.

reviewer_a_notes: This article empirically supports passive disease staging and forecasting, including application of an ADNI-derived model to an independent Geneva cohort. title: Simulating the outcome of amyloid treatments in Alzheimer's disease from imaging and clinical data.
reviewer_a_notes: Action evidence is strong because dose and timing are explicitly perturbed against natural progression. Causal evidence remains partial: effects are generated from assumed ODE structure without treatment-confounding identification. Independent-cohort validation concerns disease severity rather than intervention response, and frozen status was not verifiable because the supplement was inaccessible. No code or hazard model.
reviewer_b_notes: The paper defines a clear no-treatment versus dose/timing intervention contrast, but no treated outcomes identify that contrast. Causal evidence is therefore partial: confounding, empirical overlap, and treatment-effect validation are unavailable. Long trajectories are generated, but performance degradation is not reported at multiple rollout horizons. No code, trained parameters, formal calibration, or safety model was found.
reviewer_a_anchors: PMC8168944 Methods: 442-person ADNI cohort, latent ODE and intervention definition; Figs. 3-7 and Table 2 compare placebo with 50%/100% lowering across intervention years and sample sizes; Discussion states a conditional causal interpretation and cautions about unmodeled mechanisms; supplement link could not be retrieved.

title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
reviewer_a_notes: Despite the world-action label and motion-planning motivation, the model receives no exogenous action or robot command; it passively forecasts future visual states and observed instrument trajectories. reviewer_b_notes: The title and framing claim relevance to surgical motion planning, so coding is against planning. Decision evidence is only an offline planning proxy. The single benchmark, missing split details, no repeated-run statistics, absent uncertainty, and lack of public training code limit external and reproducibility evidence.
